summary: Observation of a spherical object with a whistling sound.
description: On December 8, 1983, at 11:27 PM, a witness heard a whistling sound similar to that emitted by a glider in flight. For 5 to 6 seconds, the witness saw a very bright, bluish-white, spherical object moving horizontally. This object was followed by a long trail of orange flames. It then disappeared into the landscape. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a circular object
description: On December 1, 1983, at approximately 10:00 PM, two witnesses observed a very bright phenomenon for a few seconds. Circular in shape and fluorescent in color, the object left trails of red and yellow behind it. It moved rapidly without changing shape or direction but appeared to lose altitude. It disappeared into the landscape. No further information could be gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of an object falling.
description: On November 26, 1983, at approximately 9:10 a.m., a motorist glimpsed, for a split second, a round object between 20 and 40 centimeters in diameter. Bright red in color and trailing a white line, the object was falling vertically at high speed. No further information or traces could be found regarding what was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On November 18, 1983, between 6 and 7 p.m., several witnesses in Moselle saw a luminous phenomenon in the sky for a few seconds. A ball, about the size of a football and orange in color, crossed the sky silently, leaving behind a long, colored trail. It was probably an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observations of an atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.
description: On November 17, 1983, between 6:30 and 7:00 PM, witnesses in three French departments (Haute-Saône, Moselle, and Meurthe-et-Moselle) saw a luminous phenomenon cross the sky. A round, brightly colored mass moved horizontally at very high speed and without any noise. The object's estimated altitude was between 1,000 and 2,000 feet. While the witnesses did not notice any change in direction during the few seconds of observation, some saw the main mass explode into several pieces of varying sizes and a reddish hue. A yellow-orange trail was also visible behind the object. These people likely witnessed a meteorite re-entering the atmosphere.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 17, 1998, three witnesses observed, at approximately 6:30 PM and for a few seconds, a luminous sphere with a trail moving very quickly along a NW-SE trajectory. These individuals likely observed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 15, 1983, between 5:00 and 6:00 a.m., witnesses in several French departments (Yonne, Seine-et-Marne, Paris, Essonne, Seine-Saint-Denis, and Pas-de-Calais) observed a peculiar phenomenon. All saw an intense, colored, luminous mass pass by at high speed. No sound was heard by the witnesses during the observations, which lasted approximately ten seconds. These individuals likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere and trace of a broken poplar on the ground: probable natural phenomenon due to parasites and tree fall.
description: On October 31, 1983, at approximately 6:45 PM, a witness, alerted by his dog's unusual barking, saw through a window, in thick fog and despite the darkness, an intense light "as big as a tractor wheel" that moved slowly and disappeared very quickly behind a curtain of poplar trees located along the riverbank. The following morning, following the witness's directions, a 25-meter-tall poplar tree was found broken at a height of 8 meters. The upper part was found on the ground among the wild vegetation, and the break was in two distinct ways. The tree had a clean break extending to the center of the trunk, followed by a tear in the wood for about two meters. The results of the analysis showed that the tree had probably been attacked for a long time by fungi that had gradually degraded it without altering its external appearance. When the decay reached the middle of the tree, its stability was compromised, and the tree was able to fall under minimal pressure. This phenomenon was exacerbated by prevailing winds, which caused general fatigue in the vegetation located between 4 and 5 meters high, thus facilitating the growth of destructive fungi. The brownish area and the layer of scar bark found at the point of breakage are consistent with this hypothesis. Regarding the bright light, one of the consulted laboratories offered an explanation. Indeed, many species of bioluminescent organisms exist in nature, including numerous fungi. These organisms can emit intense light, allowing them to illuminate a room or navigate in the dark. The hypothesis put forward is that the tree trunk, colonized by this type of organism, could have, at the time of its breakage, exposed these organisms which caused a significant glow for some time, a glow which the witness could see but could not interpret.

summary: An object moving at high speed while describing spirals.
description: On the evening of October 3, 1983, two witnesses glimpsed a luminous, circular object for a few seconds. This object moved rapidly in a straight line along a north-south axis, tracing spirals. It disappeared abruptly without a trace. No further information could be gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Presence of a light phenomenon not identified by PARIS airport radars.
description: On the night of September 28, 1983, several witnesses, including police officers, saw a luminous object in the sky. Located between 2,000 and 2,500 meters in altitude and drifting southward, the object appeared round or triangular at times. No pilots and no radar records mentioned the object, which was nevertheless photographed by the witnesses. No other information could be gathered about this sighting.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On September 26, 1983, between 6:48 PM and 7:00 PM, several witnesses observed the movement of luminous points of varying sizes and colors. This high-altitude, high-speed movement occurred silently. During the observations, which lasted from one to several minutes, these luminous points left trails of color behind them. These descriptions by the witnesses support the hypothesis of a relatively large atmospheric reentry.

summary: UFO sighting in the Polynesian sky
description: On September 26, 1983, at approximately 6:50 PM, numerous witnesses scattered throughout French Polynesia observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon. A group of six to eight very bright points of varying sizes moved at high speed from west to east, leaving luminous trails behind them. The altitude of this group was estimated at 10,000 meters. No noise related to the movement of this group was perceived during the observations. These witnesses likely observed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations of the slow movement of a point of light in the sky: astronomical observations of the planet Venus.
description: On September 26, 1983, several people observed a very bright object in the sky between 5:30 and 6:30 a.m., resembling a star to the naked eye. This object moved slowly, and observation through binoculars revealed, according to witnesses, a yellow corona surrounding a light gray crater. An examination of the star chart at the time of the observation confirmed the presence of Venus at the location indicated by the witness, with its movement precisely matching their estimate between 5:30 and 6:30 a.m.

summary: Observations by 4 witnesses of the movement of an object with flashing colored lights: probable observation of a civil or military aircraft.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named COLMARS (04) 1983, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On September 28, 1983, at approximately 9:30 p.m., four witnesses on a balcony saw intense white and red lights, "like flashes," above the mountain known as "La Femme Couchée" (The Reclining Woman). Witnesses noted that the UFO initially appeared stationary, then moved in a zigzag pattern. The UFO quickly crossed a narrow valley before disappearing towards the summit of Chalufy. The brief nature of the sighting prevented witnesses from precisely describing the object's shape. Two hypotheses were explored to explain the witnesses' observations (see the investigation report). The first involved confusion with the atmospheric reentry of an artificial object (satellite, debris). While certain aspects of the witness accounts (the brevity of the sighting, flashing white and red lights) might suggest such a phenomenon, the absence of any other reports in an urbanized area likely to have been affected by this phenomenon makes this hypothesis unlikely. Furthermore, in the catalogs that list all these atmospheric re-entries since 1958, none are identified for September 1983. The absence of a light trail is also a parameter that contradicts this hypothesis. The second hypothesis relates to simple confusion with a civilian or military aircraft observed at a relatively low altitude. This hypothesis better fits the witness accounts (particularly flashing white and red lights, and the perception of a noise), as well as the calculated data involving estimates of altitude, speed, and observation time. It is not necessarily necessary to assume that the witnesses slightly underestimated the duration of the observation. Indeed, a suitable combination of the two factors, altitude and speed, allows for a proper account of the sighting, which remains consistent both with the duration of the observation as reported by the witnesses and with the angular distance traveled by the aircraft within the limited field of vision of a narrow valley. It is therefore reasonable to conclude that this aircraft would likely have flown both faster and lower than usual in the area. This conclusion is all the more valid as this is probably what constituted the strangeness for the witnesses, who did not recognize an aircraft. Although we were able to demonstrate that civilian aircraft nowadays conduct regular flights, use air corridors, and pass through a specific SID point, all located in the immediate vicinity of the witnesses and in the observed direction, we were unable to determine whether this data was already valid in 1983, but it is nevertheless most likely that it was. The same applies to flight restriction maps, particularly those showing altitudes and heights (restricted areas). While these maps currently indicate that the area is used by military aircraft, it is highly likely that this was already the case at the time. It is not possible to favor one option over another, whether it was a military or civilian aircraft. In both cases, it is necessary to introduce an equally plausible detail: for a military aircraft, which generally flies low, it is the fact that there was an exercise that day with this particular flight path; for a civilian aircraft, which usually flies through the area, it is the fact that the altitude was lower. The evidence is consistent, with a fairly thorough investigation by the gendarmerie. It should be noted, however, that angular measurements taken on site would have allowed for a better evaluation of the hypotheses. GEIPAN classifies the case as eBe: probable sighting of a civilian or military aircraft.

summary: Periodic observation of a luminous object.
description: Between September 24 and 29, 1983, several witnesses observed a circular object in the sky, approximately 50 cm in diameter, emitting a yellowish light and rays of varying lengths. One witness, who was able to observe it with a telephoto lens, reported seeing a dark core surrounded by a bright circle. This was likely an astronomical observation. However, we lack sufficient evidence to confirm this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of several beams of light above a pavilion.
description: Between 2:00 and 2:30 a.m. on September 11, 1983, a witness observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon above his house and the surrounding houses. Cylindrical beams, one meter in diameter, brightly illuminated the houses. These eight fixed, slightly yellow bands were spaced 3 to 4 meters apart and gradually disappeared into the clouds. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a yellow-orange ball of light descending on a witness; very shocking physical effects on the witness.
description: Following several sightings of luminous phenomena at night on July 15th and 16th, 1983, a witness decided to go to a hillside around 9:30 PM on July 17th to observe what was happening with binoculars. Several hours later, his family found him at home dazed, with injuries on his body and severely traumatized. He claimed to have been struck by a yellow-orange fireball and then to have fallen a few kilometers away. His incoherent speech and injuries prompted his family to have him hospitalized. The investigation demonstrated that these luminous phenomena could indeed have occurred: a high-voltage power line belonging to EDF (the French electricity company) ran over the hill, and electrical arcs could have occurred. The witness could indeed have suffered an electric shock due to the presence of the 60 kV line and the very stormy weather, but the "abduction" explanation seems unlikely.

summary: Observation of a bright point high in the sky.
description: During the nights of July 14 and 15, 1983, several witnesses observed a bright white object in the sky, moving slowly from west to east. Despite prolonged observation, the object's precise shape and size could not be determined. The characteristics of the various observations, along with astronomical analysis of the sky on those nights, support the hypothesis of an astronomical sighting: the witnesses likely observed Venus, which was particularly visible in that area at that time.

summary: Observation of an object moving at very high speed
description: On July 15, 1983, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness observed a rounded object moving rapidly across the sky from their terrace. This green and blue object left behind a very long, sparkling white trail. The observation, which lasted about four seconds, revealed a regular and straight trajectory. The object disappeared over the horizon. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, which had the characteristics of an atmospheric reentry.

summary: observation of a high point in the sky
description: On July 14, 1983, at approximately 11:55 PM, a group of people observed the unusual movement of a point of light for 45 seconds. It moved along a north-south trajectory in short bursts, with a brightness comparable to that of a satellite. After remaining stationary for several seconds, during which the brightness increased, it reportedly moved off rapidly and disappeared over the horizon. No further information could be gathered regarding this phenomenon.

summary: Very fleeting observation of a luminous ball on the ceiling of a room with a sudden departure through the open window; stormy weather: lack of precision and cross-checking.
description: Between July 5th and 25th, 1983, around 6:00 AM, two people in a bedroom suddenly awoke with the sensation of being watched. They discovered a motionless and silent spherical ball, about the size of a handball, in a corner of the ceiling. The ball was transparent and luminous, but not dazzling. It quickly crossed the room and passed through the open window. This observation report, written in October 2013, although recounting an old memory (1983), is very precise; the analysis of the account reveals no evidence of false memory or fabrication. According to the expert from the Lightning Laboratory, the reported events closely resemble a ball lightning phenomenon. The very hot and humid weather indicated by the witness is consistent with this hypothesis. However, as the precise date of the phenomenon is unknown, and there is only one eyewitness account, GEIPAN was unable to find any evidence to confirm this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of precise information on the date. The hypothesis of a ball lightning sighting remains consistent with the witness's account.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation of the particular movements of a luminous phenomenon: lack of information.
description: Recent report (September 4, 2014) of an old sighting where the witness does not remember the date (July 1st is given arbitrarily). A witness and his wife observed the unusual movements of a luminous phenomenon in the distance. No unusual noises were heard during the 5-minute observation. Only one witness account was recorded. This sighting of a white luminous sphere, with irregular and erratic behavior, is very strange. The only plausible explanation, given the intense heat, would be a ball lightning phenomenon. As the precise date is unknown, and the observation is old (more than 30 years ago), a thorough investigation is no longer possible. This strange case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Multiple observations across southern France of the rapid passage of an elongated luminous phenomenon: probable observations of a meteoroid reentry.
description: On June 6, 1983, around 11:00 PM, numerous witnesses spread across southern France, from the Alps to the Pyrenees-Orientales, observed a rapidly moving glow in the sky at the same time (11:00 PM) and for a short duration (most often less than 20 seconds and at most 1 or 2 minutes). Twenty-nine eyewitness accounts were reported. The shape was frequently described as elongated. The table (included in the investigation materials) summarizing the locations and times of observation is striking due to its geographical extent and the corresponding time. This supports the theory of a unique phenomenon occurring at high altitude (> 50 km) and providing visibility over a wide area. This is a key characteristic of the well-known phenomenon of atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid. This is further supported by another key characteristic: the elongated glow and the short duration. A longer duration could have led to consideration of the related hypothesis of a spacecraft's atmospheric reentry. Nowadays, numerous sites record data collected on the ground (most often by automatic cameras) during these reentries, so that reports to GEIPAN are resolved without specific investigation. The 2016 example, with more than 20 recordings (included in the supplementary analysis IMO), illustrates the analogy with this earlier case of June 6, 1983, at 11:00 PM. The supplementary analysis contains a collection of witness descriptions that clearly convey the impression of rapid movement with an elongated shape. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observations of a meteoroid reentry.

summary: Long observation by 7 witnesses of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: astronomical mistake with Venus.
description: Its publications include older cases, originally classified as type C, which are now being re-examined solely to ensure more relevant conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification in an investigation report. This particular case was classified as type C in 1983 by GEPAN. On the night of May 9, 1983, between 10:30 PM and 11:30 PM, several witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky with the naked eye and binoculars. This luminosity emanated from a sphere that moved slowly and disappeared several times into the landscape. Viewed through binoculars, the shape became triangular, and different lights appeared. Seven witnesses were questioned by the gendarmerie. In the legend of the map provided by the gendarmerie, investigators indicated the "direction taken by the phenomenon" for the red arrow, when it was only the direction of observation. Witnesses reported a movement either northwest or towards Saint-Jacques, that is, to their right when looking at the object. Contact with the Saint-Michel Observatory confirmed the passage of a comet that night. However, according to astronomers, the witnesses' descriptions do not correspond to the description of the comet. This case is consistent (seven witnesses), and the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witness have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (long observation duration, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: Venus. Moreover, Venus was exactly at the angular altitude (17.5°) and azimuth (290°) described by the witnesses. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is the issue, but rather their interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (fatigue, surprise, the presence of a raised feature). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a weak strangeness is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misidentification of Venus.

summary: Observation of a round shape with portholes
description: On May 8 and 9, 1983, several witnesses observed a round shape emitting an intense white light in the sky. These observations took place between 10 PM and 3 AM. During an observation with binoculars, one witness reported seeing a round mass with portholes inside. Fog interrupted these observations, but the witnesses nevertheless saw the object move horizontally and vertically. No noise was heard. The star chart for May 8 and 9, 1983, at the indicated times, shows the presence of Venus in the observed area. However, we lack sufficient evidence to confirm the hypothesis of an astronomical observation.

summary: Observation of an ovoid luminous phenomenon moving quickly and silently: probable observation of a globular lightning phenomenon.
description: In the early hours of May 5, 1983, between 2:00 and 2:15 AM, a motorist noticed a glow on the front passenger window of his vehicle. This glow, moving up and down in all directions, intrigued the driver, who nevertheless continued on his way. Very quickly, the witness saw the glow again, this time tracing an arc before moving directly towards him on his vehicle. Seized by fear and panic, he stalled his engine and pulled over to the right shoulder of the road. The witness then noticed that the car radio was jammed and heard a loud crackling sound. The light then rose to the right and disappeared in the direction of Pau. The witness described a bluish, ovoid luminous phenomenon, 4 to 5 meters long, moving rapidly but silently and without leaving a trail. Although the driver encountered a truck driver during the initial observation, who likely also witnessed the phenomenon, only one witness statement was collected. The witness described a clear night with a cloudless, normally starry sky, but also noted that it was humid with a light southerly wind. This initially Class D observation was re-examined, and the witness statement was sent to the Lightning Research Laboratory in Cantal. The information provided by the witness now suggests the following hypothesis: this driver likely encountered a ball lightning event. The loud cracking sound heard by the witness is characteristic of ball lightning or a leading lightning strike. Furthermore, even if the dimensions given by the witness seem exaggerated at first glance, diameters of 10 to 15 meters have already been observed for this type of phenomenon. This case is class B: probable observation of a ball lightning event.

summary: Observations of a luminous phenomenon with a changing shape, bright orange in color, and seemingly following the witnesses in their movement: observations of the Blood Moon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named NAY-BOURDETTES (64) 1983, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On April 29, 1983, at approximately 11:55 PM, a couple in a car observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky, initially square-shaped, then round, and bright orange in color. The witnesses were frightened because the UFO seemed close and to be following them. They took refuge at the home of a third witness who noticed nothing unusual outside. The witness statements recorded in the police report present the characteristics of a UFO sighting (see the reconstruction). These characteristics are now well-known to GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) due to the accumulation of explained cases of this type, particularly over the last ten years (see the website www.geipan.fr and search for cases related to celestial phenomena such as Venus, the Moon, and the Sun): - observation duration of more than 30 minutes, low altitude in the sky; - the UFO's position is stable when the witness is stationary and becomes mobile as soon as the witness moves, with the perception of being followed by the UFO. This is the "following ball" illusion. The direction of the celestial body is, of course, absolutely fixed. When the car maintains a roughly constant heading, the celestial body is stationary relative to the vehicle and moves across the landscape. Since the witness was previously startled by the appearance of the UFO and perceived it to be at a close distance, this movement along the landscape is interpreted as the UFO moving parallel to the vehicle, mirroring the vehicle's speed, in this case 40 km/h above the houses. The disappearance of the celestial body behind obstacles and its reappearance at the end of a street can be seen as an intention on its part to wait for the witnesses: "There, I saw it above the CANCE establishments. It was hovering in the air and seemed to be waiting for us. Fear gripped me..." - a sensation of the UFO moving back and forth. The witness, having interpreted the celestial body as a nearby and, moreover, moving object, logically interpreted any variation in its brightness as a movement forward or backward, with the object maintaining a constant intensity. "We stopped again, and it was seeing this phenomenon moving toward us that made us reverse and flee." It was then verified that it was indeed a celestial body, namely the Moon. The direction of the Moon (0:20, azimuth 128°, elevation 6°) was indeed above the CANCE buildings, which faced the road when the witness was traveling on the La Monjoie road leaving Nay: "This time we took the La Monjoie road to try to get back to my parents' house. There, I saw it above the CANCE buildings. It was hovering in the air and seemed to be waiting for us. I was terrified..." The starting point of the misunderstanding, which led to others (following ball, back-and-forth movement), lies in the failure to recognize the celestial body. The Moon was almost full (phase 0.92) at sunrise; it was reddish, the color described for the UFO, but it did not have the classic lunar shape, neither round nor crescent. It's a common occurrence in moon misinterpretations: the presence of cloud cover in front of the moon only allows it to be seen through gaps in the clouds, whose shape is arbitrary and variable. Initially square ("suitcase," "window"), it later becomes round, but the misinterpretation has already taken hold. The weather report recorded in Lourdes-Ossun (30 km) last night indicates cloud cover (Infoclimat), and the police report mentions a call from a resident reporting having observed a glow behind a cloud in the Nay area around 11 p.m. last night, which at least confirms that the cloud cover was not total and could allow moonlight to pass through. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observations of a red moon.

summary: Probable sighting of a balloon
description: On April 25, 1983, several witnesses observed an oval-shaped object in the sky between 8:15 and 8:45 AM. Its color was light, almost transparent, and sometimes metallic or even silvery. This object moved very slowly from west to south-southwest. Several times it was obscured by clouds, eventually disappearing completely. The witnesses likely observed a balloon, possibly a weather balloon.

summary: Observation of an object descending vertically in stages: astronomical observation of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. At the initiative of a GEIPAN investigator, the case previously named LAPOUTROIE (68) 24.04.1983 was re-examined in 2013. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within a document (see Investigation Notes). On April 24, 1983, at precisely 10:20 PM, two witnesses spotted a luminous object the size of a tennis ball above a mountain range. When observed with the naked eye, the object appeared slightly ovoid, stationary with occasional slight oscillations. It was surrounded by a halo of white light. The object then descended in three successive stages, resulting in a change of color. One of the people, equipped with binoculars, observed a sphere taller than it was wide, with very bright veins on the object. It disappeared into the landscape during its descent. The new investigation demonstrates that the UFO was located exactly where Venus is. Since the sky was described by the witnesses as starry and cloudless, it is impossible that they would not have mentioned Venus next to the UFO if the latter were not Venus. The Gendarmerie investigation rejected the hypothesis of a possible astronomical error (a mistransmission of information concerning the position of Venus at the time of the observation appears to have occurred between the Gendarmerie and the contacted astronomical observatory). The credibility of the witnesses is not in question, and moreover, they were misled by a particular phenomenon of perceptual distortion (see the investigation notes). This case is classified as "A": astronomical observation of Venus.

summary: Long observations of a yellow-red glow coming from a very bright ball and oscillating in the night sky: observations of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named BUZANCY (08) 20.04.1983, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On April 20, 1983, around 11:00 PM, a farmer saw a bright red glow through a barn window. Intrigued, he went outside and observed that the brightness was coming from a ball in the sky directly above Saint-Pierremont. The witness perceived rapid movements over a short period and radiant light. After fifteen minutes, the witness called his neighbor and then the Gendarmerie. After an hour, the phenomenon was reduced to a single point of light that suddenly disappeared. Two witness statements were collected. The gendarmes participated in the end of the observation; they observed the UFO reported by the witnesses. There is little doubt that the UFO observed by the witnesses and the gendarmes was Venus (see the investigation notes). The position in the sky corresponds, and the rest of the description is typical of the misidentifications of Venus recorded in large numbers by GEIPAN. The reddish-yellow color, shining brightly among the other white stars, perfectly matches the appearance of Venus seen at low altitude. The color (generally variable, T1 describes changes) results from the effects of the thick atmosphere (low elevation). The perceptions of small, jerky movements or oscillations described by witnesses and police officers could be caused by atmospheric effects and/or by a perceptual error when staring at a star (see the article on the autokinetic effect). The sudden disappearance observed by the police around midnight could correspond to the beginning of the obstruction by the trees (visible in the background of the photo taken by the police to reconstruct the UFO's position) because Venus was now only 2 arcseconds in elevation. This could also correspond to the presence of some clouds; this hypothesis is very plausible given the meteorological analysis and could explain T1's indication of three momentary disappearances of the UFO. The other photos taken by the gendarmes to reconstruct the UFO's position in the preceding phases of the observation do not allow for this reconstruction because they do not contain any reference points or are not geolocated (the gendarmerie is unable, 35 years later, to provide this location). Nevertheless, the overall movement of the UFO, as can be inferred from the testimonies despite the errors and inconsistencies in the official report, is consistent with that of Venus. Most importantly, none of the witnesses differentiated the UFO also observed by the police at the end of the observation from another UFO that was allegedly seen earlier. It was indeed the same UFO, only much larger and closer (as stated by T1) at the beginning of the observation, which is also consistent with the fact that it was Venus at that time, higher in the sky. The testimony is marred by several inconsistencies, some of which could have contradicted the conclusion that it was Venus. Nevertheless, the analysis resolves these inconsistencies by identifying the sources of error and inaccuracies in the witnesses' or police officers' statements. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Venus sightings.

summary: Probable observation of the planet Venus
description: On April 13, 1983, between 10:45 PM and 11:05 PM, two motorists spotted a very bright sphere in the sky at a very high altitude. This sphere, about the size of a handball, was yellowish-green with variable brightness. Observed through binoculars, this sphere appeared to move rapidly vertically but never strayed more than 40 to 50 cm from its initial location, always returning. As the brightness became unbearable, the witnesses stopped observing. Examination of the star chart from the day of the observation revealed Venus quite low on the horizon (less than 5 arcseconds) in the 300 arcsecond direction, which corresponds to the angle of observation. The witnesses were therefore likely impressed by the intense brightness of the planet Venus.

summary: Observation of a shallow crater
description: Following the discovery of a crater of unknown origin in a wheat field, an investigation was launched between March and April 1983. After ruling out the hypothesis of an underground explosion due to the presence of World War II munitions, investigators focused on the possibility of a natural phenomenon. The investigation revealed that the crater formed on March 15th, the day of a major thunderstorm with a violent clap of lightning: the crater was likely formed by a lightning strike.

summary: Multiple observations of nocturnal luminous phenomena; illusion of the "following ball": observations of Venus and Arcturus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named SAINT-RENAN (29) 1983, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On March 14, 1983, between 8:00 and 10:00 PM, several witnesses in the same hamlet in the commune of Plouarzel (29) observed a yellowish luminous phenomenon that appeared stationary above the tip of a megalithic monument. The UFO was initially stationary, then began moving. Intrigued, the witnesses decided to investigate further: they were surprised because the object seemed to follow the road and the motorists. A fifth witness reported his observation the following day, March 15th, at 9 PM while driving towards Saint-Renan (29). Witness T1 arrived at their homes around 9 PM to alert witnesses T2, T3, and T4. They all stated that their initial impression upon seeing the phenomenon shown by T1 was that of a large star, and they did not understand the reason for T1's "excitement." - T2 "At first I thought it was a big star and I initially refused to believe it was a UFO. - T3 "At first I saw this bright point which appeared to me 3 to 4 times larger than a star and it emitted a bright, yellowish light." - T4 "My parents, my brothers and I went outside and Mr. Q pointed out a star in the sky to the Northwest. At first, I didn't find anything unusual. The star that T2, T3, and T4 thought they saw directly above the menhir does indeed exist, as it was Venus (272nd azimuth and 10th altitude), and it is indeed a large star. The reference to the menhir from the location of T2, T3, and T4's residence is very precise and leaves no room for doubt. T1 was very excited by his earlier observation while driving. He fell victim to the "following ball" illusion (a perceptual illusion due to the witnesses' own movement), since the UFO appears to stop when the witness is stationary and resumes its course when he starts moving again. In fact, the star's direction is fixed relative to the car when the car doesn't change course. When the car and the road change course, the star's fixed direction pivots relative to the road and can give the impression that the star is moving in the sky. T1 says, "It follows a road, making broken lines." This perception generates strong emotion (perhaps with the idea or hypothesis of dealing with an intelligence), and in doing so, can lead to a loss of precision in perception or memory. The other observations made by T1, before or after, probably result from this same phenomenon. T1, convinced of the UFO's movement, manages to get T2 into the car and naturally leads the latter to the same illusion (an illusion also fostered here by the entrainment or conditioning effect created by T1). T2 says, "It seemed to me that this phenomenon passes from one side of the road to the other." T3 and T4 remain in the yard while T2 and T1 are in the car. Upon T1 and T2's return, they perceive that the UFO has not moved, while T2 (the parent of T3 and T4) is now convinced of its movement. During a second experience in a vehicle... T2 and T1, T3 and T4 eventually saw the UFO move, but everything indicates that they themselves moved in the courtyard, because they were trying to follow the car's trajectory and the UFO's reaction (supposedly following the car; for T4, "at that moment, when my parents had traveled about a hundred meters, I clearly saw the point of light descend in the sky") and especially T3 indicates, "at one point I was blocked by a shed and I moved to follow the object's trajectory." The reference to a star-like appearance is very present in the testimonies, and anything that deviates from this is classic for Venus at low altitude and/or seen through a car windshield (changing color, oval shape, changing intensity, and the resulting impression of varying distance). The indications of the UFO's disappearance (T3, "it went towards Ushant and I never saw it again," T4, "it seems to me that this phenomenon descended quite low near of the road." perfectly correspond to the local configuration of Venus's setting. The misidentification with Venus is beyond doubt. Here we have an illustration of: - a classic initial misidentification due to the illusion of a following sphere created by the witness's movement; - a ripple effect involving other witnesses in this same illusion, other witnesses who were initially quite convinced they were seeing a star; - the emotional influence between members of the same family: T3 and T4 appropriate the idea and, through the perception of movement, once these are acquired and communicated by their relative T2. T5's testimony is poorly documented. It probably concerns the observation, the following day at 9 PM, of Arcturus at a heading of 70° in the direction followed by T5; an observation that would probably have gone unnoticed by T5 if he had not been influenced by the "facts reported in the press about the appearance of a UFO on the 14th." and March 15th." GEIPAN classifies the case as A: astronomical errors (Venus and Arcturus).

summary: Implausible sighting of a flying saucer.
description: On February 6, 1983, around 1:00 AM, a witness on a moped was passing cars when he reported being suddenly stopped by a very bright beam of light and losing consciousness. When he awoke about an hour later, he saw a very bright disc above him moving away with a noise. The witness's personality, likely due to alcohol consumption at the time, makes it difficult to take this testimony seriously.

summary: Observation of a fireball.
description: On January 29, 1983, two farmers witnessed a peculiar bluish luminous phenomenon. One of the witnesses saw a fireball the size of a balloon approaching: it moved horizontally, emitted a whistling sound, and then exploded, startling the livestock. Despite searching for traces on the ground, no further information was gathered about this phenomenon, the description of which suggested a manifestation of lightning.

summary: Observation of a spinning top-shaped object that zigzagged
description: On January 28, 1983, at 12:10 a.m., a motorist spotted a spinning-top-shaped object on his right. This craft was 2 or 3 meters above the ground and emitting faint red and green lights. The object zigzagged before spiraling high into the air and disappearing. No further information could be gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a ball moving at very high speed.
description: On January 26, 1983, between 6:55 and 7:08 AM, several witnesses in the Bouches-du-Rhône region observed a luminous white sphere moving horizontally. This sphere was followed by a colored trail. Observations lasting between 4 and 45 seconds allowed the witnesses to note the complete absence of noise and a very high speed. This phenomenon then disappeared into the landscape. No further information could be gathered about this phenomenon, which, according to eyewitness accounts, resembled atmospheric reentry.

summary: A plane will likely be observed passing overhead for 10 minutes.
description: On January 23, 1983, between 5:15 and 5:30 PM, several witnesses observed a gray-black phenomenon in the sky at an estimated altitude of 2,500 meters. The object was elongated or V-shaped and lacked brightness. It moved horizontally and silently. Observation with binoculars failed to identify the object, but according to one of the witnesses, a former flight attendant, it resembled a contrail left by a Boeing 747. The V-shape and the speed (500 to 600 km/h) estimated by the former flight attendant support the hypothesis of an aircraft seen from behind during its descent. It is likely that the witnesses mistook an aircraft for another, although it could not be identified.

summary: Observation of the fall of a luminous ball.
description: On January 12, 1983, at 6:30 PM, several witnesses observed a yellow sphere moving silently at a very low altitude. This sphere was followed by a series of small blue flames. The entire phenomenon suddenly disintegrated, leading the witnesses to believe that a fall had occurred near the observation point. Authorities were immediately notified, and several searches were conducted in the surrounding area, but to no avail. It is likely that the witnesses observed an atmospheric reentry.
